text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: paging @Priya. Alert: sustained 5xx spike and tail latency for model variant omega-v2 in us-west. 5m error rate ~7%. See metrics: https://metrics.redwood/omega-v2/alerts/12345

Alex Wang: I'm on it, running quick triage.

Priya Patel: Ack. Looking at coroutine logs on the g3-* fleet — kv-cache eviction NPEs showing up around 03:12 UTC after the kernel patch. P95 latency jumped 120ms -> 480ms. Suspect new kernel path + cache eviction race.

Rick Chen: Recommend immediate mitigation: drain/evacuate omega-v2 in us-west and route to stable-v1. Also put emergency per-key quotas for heavy tenants while we drain. I can flip routing if ops gives go.

Alex Wang: Quick question — any customer-visible semantic change when we fallback to stable-v1? We need CS note if outputs differ.

Priya Patel: Stable-v1 differs slightly (no beam-search tuning) but is functionally compatible. Customer impact = degraded novelty, not PII. 12 tenants saw elevated errors; top 3 tenants have 2-5% failures. Recommend fallback.

Jamie Li (CS): I'll draft customer comms now: "We're rerouting your requests to a stable model variant to mitigate elevated errors; you may see slight output differences." Will open tickets for affected customers and post an update on status.redwood.io if it becomes widespread.

Rick Chen: Executing routing change now — staging drain weights: 100 -> 50 -> 20 -> 0 over 2m windows.

deploy-bot: executing job:

```
POST /controlplane/api/v1/routing/variants HTTP/1.1
Host: controlplane.redwood
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "action": "demote",
  "variant": "omega-v2",
  "region": "us-west",
  "drain_policy": "staged",
  "stages": [100,50,20,0],
  "reason": "evacuate due to 5xx spike"
}
```

deploy-bot: 202 Accepted, job_id=job-6789.

incidents-bot: job-6789 started. Routing weights are updating (approx 30s between stages). Current omega-v2 traffic: 100% -> 50%

Alex Wang: I'll start applying per-key emergency quotas for heavy tenants (limit qps and short burst window). Preparing key list now.

Priya Patel: I pushed a quick quota change for top-20 heavy keys:

```
rbctl quota set --scope key --keys heavy_keys.txt --qps 10 --burst 20 --reason "evacuate omega-v2"
```

ops-bot: quotas applied for 20 keys (qps=10).

Jamie Li (CS): Notified top-3 customers via private DM. Draft posted to internal CS channel with suggested wording.

Rick Chen: Monitoring: error rate down to 1.2% after stage 2. Tail latency trending back toward baseline (P95 ~150ms). Keep watching for at least 30m.

Alex Wang: Good. Priya — can you own the pager for the next 2h? I'm stepping out for 30m.

Priya Patel: Ack handoff. I'm primary until 09:30 UTC. Will keep a 5m cadence on updates.

incidents-bot: job-6789 completed — omega-v2 drained in us-west, all traffic on stable-v1. Final check: last 5m errors 0.3%, P95 latency 130ms.

Jamie Li (CS): Status page update published: "We temporarily rerouted traffic to a stable model variant to address elevated errors for variant omega-v2 in us-west. No customer data exposure. Engineers are investigating root cause." Link: https://status.redwood.io/incidents/omega-evacuation-2026-03-14

Rick Chen: Action items being created: 1) reproduce kv-cache eviction locally, 2) roll back kernel patch on affected subset, 3) fix eviction race, 4) postmortem and follow-up rollout plan. Assigning to eng-runtime + infra.

Priya Patel: I'll start reproducibility tests and schedule a targeted revert of the kernel patch on the g3-* nodes (canary first). If revert stabilizes, we'll roll forward with proper fix.

Alex Wang: Thanks team — nice quick run. Once postmortem is drafted please link here and mark the incident resolved. :white_check_mark:

Jamie Li (CS): Opening follow-up ticket and adding customer impact summary (tenant ids, error rates, timeframe). Will update stakeholders.

Rick Chen: Leaving notes: avoid automatic rollouts for kernel patches that touch filesystem eviction paths until we have stronger canary signals.

Priya Patel: Keeping thread open until postmortem template is in place. Monitoring continues.

Alex Wang: Leaving now. Priya has the pager. :wave:

incidents-bot: incident thread will remain open for follow-ups. Recommended SLA: 72h postmortem window.
